turns.text:
ok can u edit this text to sam pls. want it polite

"hey sam, so you still owe me two saturday shifts from the september swaps.. i need you to cover one this month or give it back. thanks"

sounds kinda harsh?? 🫠

It's a little blunt, but easy to soften. Here's a friendlier version:

"Hey Sam! Hope your weekend's going well. When you get a chance, could we sort out one of the Saturday shifts from the September swaps? Whichever works for you, covering one of mine or giving one back. No rush, just want to get it on the calendar. Thanks!"

It keeps the request clear without sounding accusatory. Want it shorter or more casual?

hmm ok. still feels like a lot. can it be more like 'if you can maybe..' lol

the thing is im already on sat 6:30-1 opening every week and with mon/wed closings now i literally have no room to pick up extra. so i kinda need him to take one

Here's a softer version that still makes the need clear:

"Hey Sam! If you can, maybe you could take one of my Saturday shifts sometime this month? It'd really help, since my Mon/Wed closings leave me no room for extras. Totally fine to pick whichever date works for you. Thanks!"

Because you gave a reason, it comes across as a simple scheduling request rather than a demand.
ok wait. since hes the weekend barista who keeps swapping with me anyway.. maybe i should just take the ask out altogether?? like just say hi and see if he brings it up

I'd keep the ask in. If you only say hi, Sam may not realize you're asking, and you'd still be short on time. The softened version already sounds friendly and low-pressure.

If it helps, here's an even lighter version:

"Hey Sam! Could you maybe cover one of my Saturday shifts this month, whenever works for you? My schedule's packed with closings. Thanks so much!"

It asks for one shift and gives him room to choose the date.
ok that one. thank u!! ☕ ok im gonna eat now
Sounds good, hope it goes smoothly! Enjoy your meal.
